I'm going to give the game a bit more time, but ultimately I'm finding that gameplay is just unrewarding. The amount of times I feel like I have a good deck with synergy only to meet a boss or elite encounter that will just hard counter and destroy whatever you were going for is frustrating. That, combined with decisions throughout the gameplay that will completely fuck you over without you knowing only adds salt in the wound.

I understand a large part of roguelikes is going through run after run, but purposely obfuscating information in a roguelike to the point that you may not even understand the decision you're making unless you've made that decision before is stupid. The amount of time the game will essentially be like "I dunno, could be good could be bad aha" (legitimately, there are multiple decisions that boil down to exactly this) and you are forced to take them to even see what happens, possibly ruining a run that may have taken hours... just unfun. I've had this game dick me over with a smile on its face far more than I've felt like I've gotten any sort of upper hand. Maybe that is fun for some, but so far I can't say I'm having a great time with what feels like it should be a fun game.

I just find myself wondering when the game gets good, when the fun actually starts, why its so popular, you know?

There is a lot that has been said already in other reviews. Its a terrific , turn based game. What I can add is that this game has the distinction in my library of being the smallest hard drive size with the most amount of hours played. Its highly addictive and can play on a potato.

This game is extremely fun and has this "one more run" quality to it. So far I have been really enjoying the game and the deck building.

Heard about it, wasn't sure if it would be my kind of game, decided to give it a go, have been playing at least one run most days ever since. Easy to grasp the basics and then the more you play the more you start to unpick how all the different mechanics work and how to optimise decks in different ways and learn a little more each run.

Slay the Spire is one of the best roguelike deckbuilders out there. Its exceptionally designed and balanced gameplay makes it truly addictive to play, and slowly perfecting your strategy over the course of a run by strengthening your deck, and exploring card and relic synergies, is incredibly satisfying. The game also has an insane amount of content with four distinctly different playable characters with each their own separate card pool, which can even be expanded on through the steam workshop with quality fan made content expansions. It's a game I keep coming back to even after long periods of not playing, and I would personally recommend it to anyone (even if you usually wouldn't be into these kind of games).
I broke my arm recently, and for a while I couldn't use my left hand for anything. This game was great because it can easily be played with one hand. It got me through some hard times. 10/10.

Absolutely my Game of the Year for 2018, and it's not even in full release. I'm an avid fan of deckbuilders, and am astounded at the replayability value of Slay the Spire; there are so many plausible card and relic combinations that even with nearly 200 hours played I'm still going back for more.

The fact it's single-player only is a big plus for me, as rather than having to play a 5-15 minute online duel (that often comes with interruptions being a Dad) I can simply pause and walk away at any point, and even save at my current stage.

Honestly, for the price of a few packs of pretty much any online CCG you can get Slay the Spire in it's glorious totality. Go and buy it now.

Haven't even scratched the top layer of the surface, but I think I can safely say this game f*ckin rocks.

Edit: 70 hours later and although I still have so much to learn, I can confidently say this is in my top 20 if not top 10 favorite games of all time. Slay the Spire is a magnificent piece of art, entertainment, and borderline witchcraft. Making a game THIS good and THIS consistent is absolutely nuts.

Totally addicted! Played 100s of games over the past 30+ years, seen them all, been there, done that. But Slay the Spire has trapped me unlike any game for decades.

It's exactly the definition of a good game - "easy to play, hard to master". (unlike certain other grand strategy games, mentioning no names, but paradoxically are hard to play, easy to master) . After 200 hours of StS, I was still learning things about card interactions. Still not getting anything like the same game twice.

Only downside is that it is brutally difficult. Or at least my aged brain cells find it difficult. But every defeat is a lesson to be learnt and I do appreciate a challlenge rather than "click here for the win".

Recommended...but not if you want to do things in real life, perhaps.

Verdict: The best single-player card building roguelike. 100% recommended due to insane replay value, ascensions and how different the characters are

+
Steam trading cards (9 to create badge
Steam achievements (46, require a lot of luck and time investment)
A lot of workshop mods (even multiplayer ones!)
An incredible amount of possible builds
4 very different characters with unique playstyles (Ironclad, silent, defect and watcher)
200+ relics and items (a lot of them are unlocked by playing different characters)
350+ unique cards (+ their upgraded versions)
10 main bosses
10 elites
25 monsters (some are act unique, some are repeatable)
52 different events (each one with quite a lot of outcomes)
20 ascension levels (each adds a different game modifier)
Very high skill cap for max level plays
Endless mode
Daily runs
Custom mode
There are people with hundreds of hours for a good reason
The soundtrack is great
Remote play
Can be played on a microwave (it is that easy to run)
Doesn't take a lot of disc space (516 MB download)
Really original characters (they didn't go for fantasy clichés)

-
No real story
It may take you quite a lot of time to get into (not exactly beginner-friendly)
Random and deadly, best kind of combination; also great if have only few minutes to spare, can go back in where you last stopped

I have over 500 games on Steam, but Slay the Spire is the first ever I bought in Early Access. And, oh boy, did it deliver!

This is one of the best roguelike games I played in my life. Even though there's not much content yet, the game offers a lot of deck building possibilities and strategies. Of course, it all depends on luck: I beat the game with Ironclad on my very first try, but it took another 5 tries to finish it with The Silent. These 6 runs took me 8 hours, but I still want more and look forward for the game to get more content.

So Slay the Spire is definitely worth buying even now since the game is already very polished and provides a solid experience and a lot of fun. Moreover, the updates are frequent, so I expect the game to hit the release by summer 2018. Anyway, it can already be played for 10-20 hours before you encounter all the enemies and unlock all the cards and relics. Not bad for its price.

Update: I was wrong about 10-20 hours. It's already been 30+ and I still have one last unlock for each character.

For all the games inspired by Slay The Spire, none can match the balance, variety, replayability and depth of the original. One of those approachable games where, during your first turn you're wondering "Hmm should I swing for 6 or block for 5, that's a tough one", and then 1,000 hours later you start a new run and you're still wondering "Hmm, swing for 6 or block for 5..."

The game is so simple and addictive, it's hard to understand why it's special without playing it. Just try it for yourself!

Probably the best card roguelike game ever made. The possibilites are limitless and it's more fun every run. I strongly recommend this to people who love roguelike dungeon crawler type games or card games in general.

This game is the simplified version of card game—math addition, subtraction, multiplication, division—combined with a fun, unique visual style and some RNG elements sprinkled through to keep things fresh.

If you know what you're doing and play the right way, I'm confident you can pretty much always make it to the stage 3 boss and beat it, making it perfectly balanced up to a point where it feels that even through the RNG, you still have control over how each run goes.

The items feel fun, and building combos around them or picking/getting ones that fit your deck feels great. The game lets you take as much time as you need to decide what to do and really think your moves through, meaning a slip-up is mostly ever made by haste of your own accountability.

Overall, this is just a great wind-down game for when you wanna play something but also just watch a video or chat with friends on the side, and I could see myself or others easily losing a hundred or more hours into. I would definitely recommend Slay the Spire wholeheartedly.
